Joining the Campus Radio Station: 新生想加入校园电台,从紧张试音到主持深夜档节目的故事。

In my second month at university, I saw a poster on the noticeboard: the campus radio station was looking for new presenters. I had never spoken into a microphone before, but I wrote my name on the sign-up sheet anyway. Two days later, an email arrived inviting me to an audition.

The studio was smaller than I had imagined. A student called Priya, who had been presenting for two years, showed me how to use the mixing desk and the headphones. My voice shook during the first attempt, and I forgot to breathe between sentences. Priya just laughed and said that everybody sounds nervous at the start.

For my second attempt, I read the campus news bulletin, and this time the words flowed more naturally. A week later, I received an email: I had been accepted. My first show was a thirty-minute music programme at ten o'clock on Wednesday nights.

Now, six months on, I still get butterflies before every show. But the moment the red light goes on, I remember Priya's advice: speak to one listener, not to a crowd. Joining the station has taught me more about communication than any textbook could.
